title: Editor & simulator
description: Patch and play in your browser — the free editor & simulator needs no MusicBrain hardware and no account.

config.title: Patch it in your *browser*.
config.subtitle: Assemble a rack, patch instruments and effects, and play in your browser. Start with a ready-made patch or build your own. No MusicBrain hardware or account is required for the core editor and simulator.

items.label: no account, nothing to set up
the Teensy's C++ code, compiled to WebAssembly
projects as JSON, your own backup

config.title: Browser and Teensy
config.markdown: The simulator runs the Teensy firmware's own C++ DSP code, compiled to WebAssembly, and new modules are built for browser and Teensy together — so a patch sounds nearly the same in both places. What differs is the surroundings: audio I/O, some routing (Web Audio in the browser), and the CPU and memory a Teensy has. The **Sim** column in the editor's **Modules** tab shows which modules the simulator supports.

items.title: Synthesis
items.markdown: Subtractive, FM/DX7, wavetable, physical models and SID.

items.title: Sampling
items.markdown: Your own material, SF2 import, key/velocity zones and banks.

items.title: Effects
items.markdown: Filters, delays, modulation, reverb, compressors and EQ.

items.title: Voice & external audio
items.markdown: Vocoder, ZANG and lyric banks — each with its own requirements (banks, audio input).

items.title: Control
items.markdown: MIDI, CC and aftertouch, control surfaces. MPE is in development.

items.title: Patch tools
items.markdown: Presets and recipes; optional AI/MCP workflows with their own setup. A/B morph is a prototype.

config.markdown: *This is an overview of the project, not a list of what is in the live editor today — newer features can land in the source before they are deployed. Morph and early instrument experiments are prototypes.*

config.title: Take it to a Teensy.
config.markdown: The editor is also the front end for the hardware. To play the internal digital instruments on a **Teensy 4.1** you need a USB cable and a released firmware — no complete backplane. Check the version the device reports and start with a simple patch.
